verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const files=["lib/messaging/dispatch-audience.ts","app/(main)/nearby/actions.ts","app/(main)/admin/actions.ts"];for(const f of files){if(!fs.existsSync(f)){console.error("SCAN-717: "+f+" missing");process.exit(79)}}const guard=fs.readFileSync(files[0],"utf8");if(/from\(\W?nexus_regions\W?\)/.test(guard)||!/from\(\W?nexuses\W?\)[\s\S]*?mentor_id/.test(guard)){console.error("SCAN-717: the dispatch leadership check still looks up mentor_id in nexus_regions while hubs.nexus_id and the composer use nexuses, so a nexus mentor below janitor can never broadcast to their nexus.");process.exit(1)}for(const f of files.slice(1)){if(/from\(\W?nexus_regions\W?\)[\s\S]{0,120}mentor_id/.test(fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8"))){console.error("SCAN-717: "+f+" still resolves a nexus mentor through nexus_regions.");process.exit(1)}}'

append.detail: The lookup was wrong by table, not by column: nexuses carries mentor_id and hubs.nexus_id points at nexuses, while the guard read nexus_regions (the geography tree) and always got null. SCAN-749 moved the guard into lib/messaging/dispatch-audience.ts, shared by the create and edit paths; this change points its three lookups at nexuses, so a nexus mentor below janitor can broadcast to their nexus and to a hub or circle under it. The probe now reads the shared guard (where the behaviour lives) and the two callers, and fails if any of them resolves a mentor through nexus_regions.
